title: Free and Low-Cost Dental Care in the US: Where to Look
description: No dental insurance? Where to find free and low-cost dental care in the US: community health centers, dental schools, Medicaid, free clinic events and more.
h1: Free and low-cost dental care: where to look
intro: Millions of Americans have no dental coverage. If cost is stopping you from seeing a dentist, these options can help.

image.alt: Woman having her teeth checked by a dentist

cardText: No dental insurance? Where to find free and low-cost dental care in the US: community health centers, dental schools, Medicaid, free clinic events and more.

sections.html:
• Community health centers: federally funded health centers offer dental care with sliding-scale fees based on income. Search at FindAHealthCenter.hrsa.gov.
  • Dental schools: students treat patients under supervision, often at reduced cost. Appointments can take longer.
  • Dental hygiene schools: low-cost cleanings.
  • Medicaid and CHIP: children’s dental is covered; adult coverage varies by state.
  • Free clinic events: charitable organizations and state dental associations run free dental days.
  • Clinical trials: sometimes offer treatment at no cost.

• Ask for the practice’s cash price and any in-house membership plan.
  • Ask for a Good Faith Estimate before scheduled treatment.
  • Prioritize: treat pain and infection first, then plan the rest.
  • Consider a dental savings plan.

Swelling, fever or spreading infection needs urgent care. See our emergency dentist guide.

General information, not medical, legal or insurance advice. This post reflects the position on the date shown. Check the official sources below for the latest rules.

faqs.q: Can I get free dental care without insurance?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Free clinic events, some community health centers and charitable programs offer free care, and dental schools offer reduced-cost care.
